Millworks Technologies secures HAL Orders and Signs MoU with TridenTech for UAV Engines

✈️ Purchase Orders from HAL
Millworks has received two developmental purchase orders from Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL):
* Overhaul Division: Oxygen Valve Assemblies for the HAWK aircraft
* Engine Division, Koraput: Surge Warning Sensor Assemblies for the MiG-29, which the Company is developing for the RD-33 engine as part of its engine monitoring system.

🤝 MoU with TridenTech Engineering
Millworks has signed an MoU with TridenTech Engineering Pvt. Ltd., a Chennai-based engine design company at the IIT Madras Research Park, to co-develop, manufacture and market an Internal Combustion engine for UAVs for domestic and overseas markets.
* Millworks will lead manufacturing engineering, production and export marketing under a revenue-share arrangement
* Millworks will retain exclusive rights to the manufacturing processes it develops for engine castings, seals and key components.

EMUDHRA : EXITS GLOBAL SSL/TLS CERTIFICATE BUSINESS

• Board decided to voluntarily withdraw from the global SSL/TLS certificate business
• Global SSL/TLS is a small part of business, contributing about 1% of global revenue
• Affected CAs revoked within 14 hours of discovery; no end entity certificates issued from affected CA, infrastructure not compromised, no data breached
• Company cites rising data sovereignty and compliance complexity, cost, and large entities issuing SSL/TLS free of cost as reasons for lower business potential and RoI
• G1 RSA roots to serve customers until transition is complete; affected customers to get free certificate replacement from partners; remaining browser root program commitments including full root-cause report to be completed
• Core businesses unaffected - DSC, eSign and other signing services in India, enterprise PKI (emCA, CertiNext), emSigner and identity solutions (SecurePass, emAS) continue normally
Impact: Neutral (exit covers only ~1% of global revenue while sharpening focus on core enterprise solutions and trust services; no breach or infrastructure compromise stated)

SWIGGY Q2: INSTAMART INVENTORY OWNERSHIP SHIFT COULD BOOST CONTRIBUTION MARGIN BY 80 BPS

• Regulatory Milestone: Swiggy secured necessary approvals to transition into an Indian-owned and controlled company (IOCC)

• Domestic Ownership: Indian shareholding increased to over 58%, with foreign ownership capped at 49.5% on a fully diluted basis

• Transition Timeline: Inventory ownership transition to begin in mid-Q3 FY27, with completion expected over the following 2–3 quarters

• Margin Expansion: New inventory ownership model could improve Instamart's contribution margin by approximately 80 bps after full implementation

• Operational Control: Greater flexibility over product assortment, pricing, inventory availability and daily operations

• Working Capital: Management expects an 8–10 day improvement in the working capital cycle, with steady-state net working capital at approximately 15 days

• Capital Requirement: No significant incremental working capital deployment expected despite inventory moving onto the balance sheet

• Business Continuity: Management expects no disruption to customer experience or supplier relationships during the transition

SWIGGY Q2: INSTAMART'S PRIVATE BRAND NO!CE GAINS TRACTION; SWITCH PRODUCTS FEATURE IN 20%+ ORDERS

• Switch Growth: Differentiated products featured in over 20% of Instamart orders, spanning 60+ categories

• Brand Partnerships: Collaborating with around 400 brands through Switch to offer differentiated products

• No!ce Expansion: Clean-food private brand featured in more than 1 in 8 orders, with over 500 SKUs

• Higher Retention: Customers purchasing No!ce showed 15 percentage points higher retention

• Margin Improvement: No!ce products are margin-accretive, supporting better profitability through premium-quality offerings

• Nectr Launch: Curated fruits and vegetables brand launched in Bengaluru during Q2 FY27

📢 Business Update – Patel Retail Limited

📍 Finalises Two New Store Locations; Enters Nashik District

Patel Retail Limited (BSE: 544487 | NSE: PATELRMART) has finalised two locations for its upcoming stores at Ghoti in Nashik district and Mangaon/Mahad in Raigad district, as part of its ongoing retail expansion plans.

🏬 New Market Entry: The proposed Ghoti store will mark the Company’s entry into Nashik district, expanding its retail presence across four districts — Thane, Raigad, Palghar and Nashik.

📍 Strengthening Existing Markets: The upcoming location at Mangaon/Mahad will further strengthen the Company’s presence in Raigad district.

📈 Business Impact: With an existing network of 54 stores, the planned additions align with Patel Retail’s cluster-based expansion strategy, targeting underserved markets with limited organised retail presence. Aditya Kumar Halwasiya Invests ₹174.92 Crore in PC Jeweller as Company Reports Strong Earnings Growth and Achieves Debt-Free Status

Mr. Aditya Kumar Halwasiya has further strengthened his investment in PC Jeweller Limited with the purchase of 5.51 crore shares worth approximately ₹101.33 crore on October 21, 2026, at ₹18.39 per share. This follows his earlier acquisition of 5.10 crore shares worth ₹73.59 crore on October 15, 2026. Across both transactions, he has acquired 10.61 crore shares for a combined investment of approximately ₹174.92 crore.

The investment comes amid PC Jeweller’s strong financial performance in Q2 FY27. The company reported sales of ₹1,054 crore, up 28% year-on-year, while Gross Profit increased 68% to ₹325 crore. Operating EBITDA rose 74% to ₹310 crore, and Operating PAT increased 107% to ₹299 crore. For H1 FY27, sales grew 25% to ₹1,932 crore, while Operating PAT increased 129% to ₹512 crore.

Operationally, PC Jeweller achieved debt-free status after clearing its outstanding dues to all 14 consortium banks on September 25, 2026. The company also received approximately ₹142 crore from export debtors during Q2 FY27, marking the beginning of realisation of long-pending export receivables.

Looking ahead, PC Jeweller plans to establish up to 100 large-format showrooms across Tier I, II and III cities over the next 12–18 months. It is also developing a new jewellery brand targeting younger consumers and advancing its gold mining project in Chad, supporting its expansion and backward integration plans.

**LTM – ICICI SECURITIES**
#Q2FY27
**Rating: REDUCE**
**Target Price: ₹3,720 (CMP: ₹4,235)**

**Financial Performance**
- Q2FY27 revenue stood at US$1,235.2 Mn, up 1.1% QoQ.
- AI revenue grew 12.7% QoQ.
- AI contributed 13.4% of total revenue.
- Non-AI revenue declined 0.6% QoQ.
- EBIT margins remained broadly stable and in line with estimates.

**Deal Pipeline & Growth**
- Deal TCV declined 25% QoQ and 20.8% YoY.
- Shift towards shorter-tenure AI deals reduced reported TCV.
- Management targets approximately 6% organic USD revenue growth in FY27.
- ICICI Securities views achieving this target as challenging.
- Weak non-AI revenue remains a key concern.

**AI Strategy & Investments**
- Launched BlueVerse One Token and BlueVerse RightLogic.
- Expanded AI partnerships with Anthropic and IBM.
- AI engagements offer better gross-margin potential.
- Management aims to maintain FY27 organic EBIT margins near FY26 levels.

**Other Business Updates**
- H1 growth came mainly from outside the top five clients.
- Top-five client revenue has started returning to growth.
- Headcount increased by 949 to 88,835 employees.
- Added 1,743 freshers during the quarter.
- Operating cash flow declined due to gratuity provisions and advance tax payments.

**Valuation & Brokerage View**
- ICICI Securities maintains REDUCE with a ₹3,720 target.
- Current price: ₹4,235.
- Valuation stands at approximately 20x FY27E P/E.
- FY27E EPS estimated at ₹205.1.
- Brokerage cites stretched valuation and uncertain growth delivery.

**Key Takeaway**
- AI revenue is growing, but non-AI business remains weak.
- Lower deal TCV raises concerns over future revenue visibility.
- FY27 growth guidance appears challenging to achieve.
- Impact: **Negative**

**CROMPTON GREAVES CONSUMER ELECTRICALS – ICICI SECURITIES**
#Q2FY27
**Rating: BUY (Maintained)**
**Target Price: ₹270 (Earlier: ₹315)**

**Financial Performance**
- Revenue grew 18.2% YoY, marking the third consecutive quarter of double-digit growth.
- EBITDA increased 24.1% YoY.
- Adjusted PAT rose 30.6% YoY.
- FY27E revenue estimated at ₹9,197 Cr.
- FY27E EBITDA estimated at ₹960 Cr.
- FY27E adjusted PAT estimated at ₹601 Cr.
- FY27E EPS estimated at ₹9.3.

**Segment Performance**
- Fans delivered double-digit growth.
- BLDC fan sales surged 40% YoY.
- ECD revenue grew 19.4%; EBIT increased 30.7%.
- Lighting revenue increased 14.3% YoY.
- Rooftop solar and wires businesses progressed well.
- Export revenue rose over 70% to a record quarterly high.

**Margins & Cost Management**
- Cumulative price hikes reached 11–16% across categories.
- Around 80% of cost inflation has been passed on.
- Further pricing and Project Unnati savings may offset remaining inflation.
- Operating leverage supported profitability growth.

Curious when FII will come back to India

So gave Co-pilot a prompt
“Why FIIs wont return to India even as AI trade unwind globally”

Reverse Psychology

Here is the response

1. India is still expensive vs EM peers
o Even after corrections, India trades at a premium to most emerging markets.
o FIIs compare India with China, Korea, Taiwan, Brazil, not with India's own history.
o If China is at 10-12x PE and India at 20-25x PE, capital tends to chase cheaper markets. 
2. India lacks direct AI beneficiaries
o The AI trade created winners in US tech, Taiwan semiconductors and Korean memory-chip companies.
o India has very few large listed AI, semiconductor or hyperscaler plays that global thematic funds can buy. 
3. Dollar returns matter, not rupee returns
o FIIs think in USD.
o Even if Nifty is flat or slightly up, rupee depreciation can wipe out returns.
o Currency risk remains a major deterrent for foreign capital. 
4. US yields remain a strong competitor
o If US Treasuries offer attractive risk-free returns, FIIs need a much higher expected return from India.
o Many global allocators prefer earning 4-5% in dollar assets rather than taking EM risk. 
5. India's earnings growth has moderated
o India's premium valuation was justified when earnings were compounding rapidly.
o If earnings growth slows while valuations remain rich, FIIs question the risk-reward. 
6. Better opportunities elsewhere
o Korea, Taiwan and China offer exposure to AI, semiconductors and manufacturing at lower valuations.
o Global funds have finite capital; India is competing against these markets for allocation. 
7. India is no longer an under-owned market
o After years of strong inflows, most EM funds already have meaningful India exposure.
o Incremental flows require a new catalyst, not just the absence of AI enthusiasm.
8. Domestic flows reduce urgency
o SIPs, mutual funds and insurance money continue supporting Indian markets despite FII selling.
o Paradoxically, this resilience prevents large valuation corrections that would otherwise attract FIIs back.

Maruti Suzuki India should be rechristened as Suzuki India

Maruti's journey started as a Govt of India project. Maruti Udyog was the Indian promoter & Suzuki was brought in as the technology partner. Back then, this was very much an Indian company with Japanese know-how.

Over time, the Indian promoter gradually diluted its holding & eventually exited completely. Suzuki did the opposite, staying invested through every cycle & steadily increasing its stake.

What began as a JV slowly became Suzuki's most important global asset. The ownership story itself tells you who has deepened commitment over the decades.

For years, investors debated why Suzuki was setting up fresh manufacturing capacity outside Maruti Suzuki through its Gujarat subsidiary instead of housing it directly in the listed entity.

Then came the reversal. Suzuki transferred Suzuki Motor Gujarat into Maruti Suzuki at a valuation of roughly ₹12,000+ Cr. Rather than taking cash, it largely took equity.

The result? Suzuki's ownership in Maruti Suzuki moved up further without having to buy equivalent shares from the secondary market.

This wasn't just a restructuring exercise. It was Suzuki effectively converting manufacturing assets into a larger stake in India's largest PV company.

Even after that transaction, Suzuki did not stop. It has periodically picked up additional shares from the open market whenever opportunities emerged.

The message is clear. The Indian promoter exited long ago. The Japanese promoter keeps doubling down on India.

Look at the cars on the road today. The branding emphasis is on the giant "S" logo. 10-15years back, cars started selling with only “S” logo, 1st on premium nexa cars, then on all the models. You will hardly see Maruti branded cars on road now

For many younger buyers, the brand recall is shifting from "Maruti Suzuki" to simply "Suzuki". The transition is subtle but visible.

India is now the crown jewel of Suzuki Motor Corp. A substantial portion of Suzuki valuation come from Indian listed entity. Maruti $38bn mcap translate to $21bn (for 58% stake, $15bn if applied 30% Holdco disc).

Even beyond that, Maruti pays over $500m to Suzuki as royalty, that value must be over $5bn in the SoTP of Suzuki motors. Suzuki motors also have successful 2w biz in India, they are 6th largest 2w in India, clocking over 1lac units every month

In many ways, investors buying Suzuki Motor Corp are indirectly buying the India story. Cars sold by Suzuki in India is higher than overall car sold by Suzuki in other 100 countries combined

A rebranding to "Suzuki India" could also help shed the old "cheap small-car company" perception. As premium SUVs, hybrids & future EVs gain share, a stronger global MNC identity may command a different customer mindset.

Ownership, capital allocation, manufacturing integration, branding & growth strategy all point in one direction: this is increasingly Suzuki's India story.

Conclusion: Maruti only stays in Co. name hence should be renamed now

What regulators see that investors often ignore 👇

Every time a regulator acts, investors first ask: "How much EPS gets hit?" Regulators ask something else: "Is the market structure fair for the end consumer?" That's a very different lens. 
Thoughts on recent #PBFintech & older #IEX n more

Case in point: Recent change on insurance commissions. The proposed changes effectively aim to reduce distribution costs & curb excessive upfront payouts on some products. Investors see lower margins. Regulators see lower customer acquisition costs & better value for policyholders.

Truth is, hardly anyone argues that insurance has zero mis-selling. Higher upfront commissions have often created incentives to sell what pays the most, not what suits the customer best. If that problem exists, intervention shouldn't be surprising.

The irony is that many investors celebrate efficiency in every industry except their own portfolio holdings. When a regulator targets excess distribution costs, the reaction is often outrage instead of introspection.

Look at insurance expense ratios. Even as the industry scaled up, commission/expense pools as a % of premium remained elevated in several segments. The regulator's job is to ask: why isn't scale translating into lower customer costs?

Learning from MFs TER. Every TER cut was seen as fatal attack. Prediction was: growth will die, distributors will vanish, profit collapse. Instead industry adapted. Players became efficient, direct plans gained share, technology reduced costs, investor participation & AUM surged

Market coupling in power exch. Investors focus: which exchange lose market share. Regulators focus: consumers get better price discovery. Market coupling means bids/orders from all exch get pooled to discover a single price. One price improves efficiency & reduces fragmentation

Could one exchange lose moat? Maybe. But from system perspective, better price discovery, deeper liquidity & lower market distortion are hard to ignore.
Regulators rarely optimize for shareholder returns. They optimize for consumers, market efficiency & long-term public interest

Think about hospitals. If tomorrow there is stricter price regulation, hospital stocks may get hit. As investors we'd feel the pain. But can anyone honestly deny healthcare costs are becoming unaffordable for a large section of Indians?
One may argue India's healthcare is still cheaper than many countries. True. But the person comparing prices globally is not the same person struggling to pay a hospital bill locally.

Markets often assume regulators must protect industry profitability. Regulators believe industries shouldn't fleece poor customers. When public benefit & industry profits collide, the regulator's choice is usually obvious.

That's why stock market reaction is often the last variable in the regulator's decision. If a policy improves consumer outcomes, transparency, affordability or efficiency, temporary shareholder pain rarely changes the outcome.
